messages:
alexc: heads-up: I ran a microbench across flash-hybrid vs paged-fused on the bf16 interleaved KV layout and hit a ~18% regression for seq_len=1024, batch=8 vs the previous baseline.
kim-ng: can you paste the numbers and the profiler flame? was this on the canary kernel-selector change?
alexc: yep canary selector (thresholds adjusted to prefer flash-hybrid for batch>=4). raw numbers below:  
```
Baseline (flash-variant A, separate-kv, bf16):  token/s=12500   p50=28.3ms
Canary (paged-fused, interleaved-kv, bf16): token/s=10250   p50=33.4ms
Env: A100, driver 525, cudnn 8.9
```
sara-m: interesting — interleaved KV + bf16 + paged layout combo has historically had alignment/stride sensitivity. did you check stride mod 64?
alexc: good call. I re-ran with a debug dump. When the kv stride is not 64-aligned (stride%64==16) we see extra copies in the fused path. profiler snippet: 
```
[GPU] copy_kernel                     36.2%
[GPU] flash_attn_fused                48.1%
[GPU] paged_kv_page_walk              11.4%
```
juan-p: that paged_kv_page_walk spike means page churn + memcpy. probably falling back to a slow path that materializes pages into aligned buffers.
kim-ng: could be the kernel selection logic misclassifying interleaved bf16 as safe for fused page path. selector checks: dtype==bf16 && layout==interleaved -> pick paged-fused. but we didn't include stride alignment in heuristics.
alexc: proposal: change selector to require kv_stride % 64 == 0 for paged-fused, else prefer separate layout or flash-hybrid with an extra alignment-copy inside runtime. low-risk flag: `runtime.features.paged_fused_require_aligned_stride` default=false.
sara-m: alternative: add a small padding allocator that rounds up stride to 64 in-place for interleaved layout when memory permits. cheaper than full layout fallback for big batches.
juan-p: padding allocator might blow memory for very long contexts. we should measure memory delta for seq=4096. also test uint8/quantized paths; int8 kernels behave differently.
perf-bot: perf job queued: /perf/jobs/1969876543: tests = [seq:512,1024,2048,4096] x [batch:1,4,8,16] x [layout:interleaved,separate] x [dtype:bf16,float16,int8] x [selector:canary,baseline]
kim-ng: thanks perf-bot. immediate action: alex, can you add a small reproducer script and a short runbook in the issue? label: perf/regression, priority:high. i'll hold the selector rollout until we see the job matrix.
alexc: will do. quick reproducer snippet I used: 
```
# run on test machine
python perf_runner.py --model small --seq 1024 --batch 8 --dtype bf16 --kv_layout interleaved --kernel paged_fused --iters 200
```
sara-m: one more ask: capture the kernel-launch args (grid/block) and the first-few bytes of the KV stride variable in the perf run artifacts. helps root cause whether it's allocator vs kernel alignment assumption.
juan-p: and add a microbench for batching heuristics: vary accumulated_batch_tokens and see when selector flips. that threshold may be masking the layout issue for some traffic shapes.
alexc: noted. i'll open issue and attach traces + reproducer. will coordinate a canary rollback if perf-job confirms regression. :thumbsup:
kim-ng: thanks team — looping in runtime-oncall if perf confirms.
perf-bot: job finished (partial): early results show the regression reproduced for bf16+interleaved at seq>=1024. full artifacts: /perf/artifacts/1969876543.zip
alexc: got it. creating issue now: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/RWI-3221 (perf/regression: paged-fused + interleaved + bf16)
sara-m: good. after fix we should add a unit test in kernel-selector that asserts selection boundary for stride alignment.
juan-p: and add a small e2e in CI that runs the reproducer on a single GPU weekly to catch regressions.
kim-ng: perfect. closing the loop once we have the canary results.
